args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001.

1. **Diagnosis:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west and eu-west), with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.
2. **Rollback:** All three regions now run v2.3.0. A follow-up status check shows the service healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** The SEV2 incident for checkout-api is INC-0001. It says what failed, the rollback to v2.3.0 and how the service looks now. It also notes that the v2.3.1 test build was already failing in staging before it went to production. The first request to create the incident timed out, so I checked the incident list before trying again. The incident had been created, so there's only one and the on-call engineer was paged once.

No change-manager approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production. Next, someone needs to find out why v2.3.1 failed before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
